# Results — Study 619 (BITO Roll Drag)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
futures-based bitcoin ETF pays a toll every month it rolls: measurable daylight between BITO
and spot** — run on the full BITO tape (inception 2021-10-19) against spot bitcoin, and on the
clean matched-close race against the spot ETF IBIT once it listed (2024-01-11). All legs are
**total-return** (yfinance `auto_adjust`; BITO pays very large monthly distributions, so a
price-only tape would wildly overstate the drag). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `48e3e370f939`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **total-return** closes: `BITO` (CME front-month futures ETF), `IBIT` (spot ETF, 2024-01-11+), `BTC-USD` (spot), `BTC=F` (CME front future — used only to classify contango) |
| Window | 2021-10-20 → 2026-06-30 (**4.69** years; 1,177 rows, 1,176 daily gaps; 56 complete months) |
| Alignment | spot sampled on BITO's trading days (weekend crypto moves fold into Monday — the same window BITO's own Friday→Monday return spans) |
| Timestamp caveat | Yahoo's BTC-USD closes ~00:00 UTC vs BITO/IBIT 16:00 ET — noise on *daily* gaps vs spot (it attenuates the daily beta to 0.947 and inflates the daily HAC SE) but no bias in means: the IBIT-vs-spot control reads **+0.28%/yr, t = +0.10**. The BITO-vs-IBIT race is matched-close and free of it (beta 1.003) |
| Execution / lag | the drag is a passive-holding identity (no signal, no lag); the one documented lag is the **prior-day basis sign** in the regime split and the prior-close entry of the always-on spread |
| Survivorship | none — single instrument, still listed; nothing was selected on survival |

## The headline — the toll is real, on both rulers

| race | window | drag (ann.) | t | cumulative |
|---|---|--:|--:|---|
| **BITO vs spot** (daily) | 2021-10-20 → 2026-06-30 | **−4.25%/yr** (−1.69 bps/day) | HAC(21) *t* = −1.67 (timestamp-noisy) | BITO **−31.45%** vs spot **−11.26%** → shortfall **−20.18 pp**, wealth ratio **0.773** |
| **BITO vs spot** (monthly) | 56 complete months | **−34.49 bps/month** | **HAC(3) *t* = −2.32** | **69.6%** of months negative |
| **BITO vs IBIT** (matched closes) | 2024-01-11 → 2026-06-30 (617 days) | **−5.14%/yr** (−2.04 bps/day) | **HAC(21) *t* = −7.68** (HAC(5) −7.22, HAC(63) −7.27) | BITO **+9.99%** vs IBIT **+25.01%** → shortfall **−15.02 pp**, wealth ratio **0.880** |
| IBIT vs spot (control) | same window | +0.28%/yr | *t* = +0.10 | the spot ETF tracks within noise |

A BITO dollar held since inception is worth **77.3 cents** of the spot-bitcoin dollar. In the
spot-ETF era the clean matched-close race certifies the toll at ***t* = −7.68**: **−5.14%/yr**,
of which **0.70%/yr** is the fee gap (BITO ER 0.95% vs IBIT 0.25%) and **~4.44%/yr** is the
roll/carry toll — almost exactly the **median annualized front-month basis of +4.90%/yr**
measured on the same tape. The arithmetic closes.

## Roll-window attribution — the toll is NOT paid at the roll

Window = the 5 trading days ending on each month's expiry Friday (CME bitcoin futures terminate
the last Friday; BITO rolls into expiry).

| race | in-window (bps/day) | outside (bps/day) | Welch *t* | window share of days / of shortfall |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| vs spot | −4.14 (n=285) | −0.91 (n=891) | −0.33 | 24.2% / 54.6% |
| vs IBIT | −2.84 (n=150) | −1.78 (n=467) | −0.87 | 24.3% / 33.6% |

No significant concentration in expiry week. That is exactly what a **carry** mechanism
predicts: the future is bought at a premium and *converges to spot a little every day* — the
roll trade itself is P&L-neutral. "Pays a toll every month it rolls" is right about the size
and the monthly cadence, wrong about the *where*: the toll accrues daily, the roll only resets
the meter.

## Contango / backwardation — the sign of the carry

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| share of days in contango (front basis > 0) | **58.5%** |
| median front basis | **+19.1 bps** at mean **13.9** days to expiry |
| median annualized front basis | **+4.90%/yr** (2022: **−4.72%** ; 2024-26: **+7.16%**) |

Calendar-year monthly gap vs spot (complete months):

| year | bps/month | months | cumulative |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2021 | −163.2 | 2 | −3.24 pp |
| **2022** | **+33.3** | 12 | **+3.63 pp** |
| 2023 | −56.4 | 12 | −6.60 pp |
| 2024 | −56.9 | 12 | −6.78 pp |
| 2025 | −43.7 | 12 | −5.14 pp |
| 2026 (H1) | −20.0 | 6 | −1.20 pp |

The drag **flipped sign in 2022** — the one backwardated year (median annualized basis −4.72%),
BITO *beat* spot by +3.63 pp — and has been negative every year since the curve went back into
contango. Directionally this is the carry story, but the year contrast (+33.3 vs −47.7 bps/mo,
2022 vs 2023+) reads **Welch *t* = +0.98** on 12-vs-42 noisy months — *suggestive, not
certified*. The daily lag-1 basis-sign split (vs IBIT: contango −6.16%/yr vs backwardation
−3.35%/yr, Welch *t* = −1.09) is underpowered — and the synthetic control shows that flavor of
split is artifact-prone (AR(1) basis noise mean-reverts into the gap), so we do not lean on it.

## Tradability — long IBIT / short BITO, dollar-neutral, daily rebalance

Short pays borrow on full notional; 2 bps one-way on rebalancing turnover; positions from the
prior close. Spot-ETF era only (before 2024-01-11 there was no clean long leg).

| borrow | gross (ann.) | net (ann.) | HAC *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0%/yr | +5.14% | +4.90% | +7.34 | +2.55 |
| **2%/yr** | +5.14% | **+2.90%** | **+4.34** | **+1.51** |
| 5%/yr | +5.14% | **−0.10%** | −0.16 | −0.05 |

Spread vol **1.92%/yr**, worst day **−0.56%** (617 days). The active harvest is real at cheap
borrow and **dies entirely by ~5% borrow**; the absolute carry is thin (~3%/yr net) and capacity
is bounded by BITO's float. The *risk-free* expression — simply holding the spot ETF instead of
the futures ETF — is available to anyone since Jan-2024, but that is **cost avoidance, not
alpha**.

## Third axis — post spot ETFs, is there ANY reason BITO survives?

On the tape: none that shows up in returns. BITO's beta on IBIT is **1.003** — the *same*
exposure — while paying **−5.14%/yr** (*t* = −7.68). Its famous monthly "income" distributions
are the futures gains handed back (already reinvested in our total-return legs — the −5.14%/yr
is *after* crediting them); an income wrapper on your own capital is optics, not yield. The two
historical frictions that justified BITO — first-mover access in 40-Act accounts (Oct-2021,
pre-spot-approval) and the only listed ETF option chain — expired when the spot ETFs listed
(Jan-2024) and IBIT options followed (Nov-2024, now the deeper chain). What remains is
habitat: legacy positions, mandates written before 2024, and its established options market.
**Busted** as a *performance* rationale.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful *(never market evidence)*

Deterministic GBM spot + front-month curve with a planted annualized basis + fee and AR(1)
basis noise; the futures-ETF NAV rolls at each expiry.

| planted drag | measured | HAC *t* | roll-window Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 (basis 0, fee 0) | +0.22%/yr | +0.70 | +0.20 |
| **−10.95%/yr** (basis 10% + fee 0.95%) | **−10.42%/yr** | −32.55 | +0.11 |

The detector recovers a planted toll (95% of it; the residual is calendar-vs-trading-day
annualization) and does **not** invent one from basis noise; the planted drag is diffuse across
the month by construction, matching the real tape's roll-window verdict. The control also
*exposed a trap*: conditioning the daily gap on the lagged basis sign manufactures a huge
spurious split from mean-reverting basis noise alone — which is why regime attribution above
leans on calendar-year basis levels instead.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The toll is on the tape twice over: **−34.49 bps/month** vs spot over 56
  months (HAC *t* = **−2.32**, 69.6% of months negative, −20.18 pp cumulative) and, on the
  clean matched-close ruler, **−5.14%/yr** vs IBIT (HAC(21) *t* = **−7.68**, lag-robust). The
  decomposition closes: 0.70% fee gap + ~4.44% carry ≈ the +4.90%/yr median annualized front
  basis. Clears *t* ≥ 2 on the real tape. No survivorship (single live instrument).
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The passive fix (hold the spot ETF) is free but is cost avoidance,
  not alpha — and didn't exist before 2024 (which is *why* BITO gathered assets). The active
  harvest (long IBIT / short BITO) nets **+2.90%/yr at HAC *t* = +4.34, Sharpe 1.51** at 2%
  borrow — real, but thin, capacity-bounded, and **it dies at ~5% borrow** (−0.10%/yr). The
  drag itself flipped sign in the 2022 backwardation — the toll is a contango phenomenon, not a
  constant of nature.
- **"Any reason BITO survives the spot ETFs?" — BUSTED.** Same beta (1.003 on IBIT), −5.14%/yr
  toll, *t* = −7.68; the "monthly income" is your own capital repackaged (the drag is measured
  *after* crediting every distribution); the access and options rationales migrated to the spot
  ETFs by Nov-2024. What's left is habitat and habit, not performance.
